extracted.intended_audience: Prospective NASA ROSES proposers, peer reviewers, and NASA Program Officers (research scientists applying to or evaluating ROSES proposals)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and criteria for peer review and selection of proposals submitted to NASA's ROSES program, describing the standard evaluation criteria, review process, adjectival ratings, and selection recommendation factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intrinsic Scientific or Technical Merit of the Proposed Work
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates the strength of the science questions, hypotheses, and goals; whether the methodology is sound and appropriate; the qualifications of the proposing team; and the Open Science and Data Management Plan (OSDMP) if required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the page: 'The strength of the science questions, hypotheses, and goals; Whether the methodology is sound and appropriate; The qualifications of the proposing team; Open Science and Data Management Plan (OSDMP) - if required, evaluated as part of intrinsic merit.' This criterion is one of three standard evaluation criteria and drives the scientific/technical component of the panel rating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance of the Proposed Work to NASA
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses alignment with NASA's strategic goals, relevance to the specific program element being applied to, and use of and contribution to NASA missions, datasets, models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the page: 'Alignment with NASA's strategic goals; Relevance to the specific program element being applied to; Use of and contribution to NASA missions, datasets, models.' Relevance is explicitly a standard evaluation dimension and also factors into program officer selection recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability of the Proposed Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges cost reasonableness, cost realism, and whether the proposed costs are commensurate with the scope of work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the page: 'Cost reasonableness; Cost realism; Are the proposed costs commensurate with the scope of work?' This financial suitability is the third standard evaluation criterion used by reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review Panel Evaluation Factors and Panel Composition Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review panels evaluate proposals based on scientific and technical merit, perceived programmatic relevance, and cost reasonableness; a minimum of three unconflicted and unbiased panel reviewers shall contribute to the panel rating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the page: 'A peer review panel comprised of reviewers with expertise relevant to the content of the proposal evaluates the proposal based on: Scientific and technical merit; Perceived programmatic relevance; Cost reasonableness. A minimum of three unconflicted and unbiased panel reviewers shall contribute to the panel rating.' This is both an evaluative checklist and a procedural requirement about reviewer composition/number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjectival Ratings (merit scale and interpretation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each criterion receives an adjectival rating: Excellent, Very Good, Good, Fair, or Poor; ratings are often summarized into groupings (E/VG = high merit; G = competitive with weaknesses; F/P = generally not selectable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the page: 'Each criterion is given a rating: Excellent, Very Good, Good, Fair, or Poor, often summarized into: E/VG = high merit (likely selectable); G = competitive but with weaknesses; F/P = generally not selectable.' Use these adjectival ratings to summarize reviewer judgments and to inform selection decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Officer Selection Recommendation Factors
rubrics_metrics.description: A NASA Program Officer develops a recommendation based on the peer review, any program-unique criteria stated in the funding announcement, relevance to objectives stated in the funding announcement and to NASA's strategic goals, comparison with competing proposals of equal merit, and available resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the page: 'A NASA Program Officer develops a recommendation based on: The peer review; Any program-unique criteria stated in the funding announcement; Relevance to objectives stated in the funding announcement and to NASA's strategic goals; Comparison with competing proposals of equal merit; Available resources.' This describes non-merit factors and tie-breaking/selection tradeoffs used after peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual-Anonymous Peer Review (DAPR) process
rubrics_metrics.description: For many ROSES programs, NASA uses dual-anonymous peer review: reviewers do not know the identity of proposers during the initial scientific evaluation; identifying information about proposers is added only after merit assessment is complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the page: 'NASA uses DAPR for many ROSES programs. Reviewers do not know the identity of proposers during the initial scientific evaluation. Identifying information about proposers is added only after merit assessment is complete.' This procedural rule affects how proposals should be prepared (i.e., remove identifying information where required) and how reviews are conducted.
